item.title: The Travel Industry Needs a New Way to Read OTA Results
item.description: OTAs posted double-digit growth in the latest earnings cycle even as consumer travel spending declined. The industry needs a new framework for reading these results — and the signals that actually matter.

item.title: Has JetBlue’s Transatlantic Growth Hit a Ceiling?
item.description: JetBlue’s transatlantic ambitions are beginning to meet practical limits. Summer 2026 reflects an airline fine-tuning growth as slot constraints, fleet availability, and intensifying competition test its model.

item.title: Meliá’s Upmarket Bet Pays Off in Spain. Cuba Is Another Story
item.description: Meliá is benefiting from Spain’s tourism boom, but Cuba highlights how quickly local conditions can pressure performance.

item.title: Bilt Taps Luxury Hotels to Build Marketplace for Top Spenders
item.description: Bilt is trying to thread a needle in building a hotel booking platform without becoming an OTA that hotels resent. One of its tactics is to offer spending data on its most loyal customers to help luxury hotels provide personalized service for first-time guests.

item.title: IAG Sees U.S. ‘Rebound’ – Even Economy Travel is Stabilizing
item.description: Premium travelers are still driving profits, but improving economy bookings suggest the North Atlantic market is more resilient than some feared.

item.title: Pets In, Kids Out: The Travel Industry’s Quiet War on Families
item.description: With U.S. birth rates at record lows and pet ownership soaring, the travel industry is simply following the demographic money.

item.title: Too Many Brands: Hotel Groups Chased Scale. Now They Need Focus
item.description: Hotel companies built portfolios for coverage and growth. In an AI-compressed, loyalty-fatigued market, the next competitive edge will come from sharper brands, not more of them.

item.title: Amadeus Sets First Multi-Year Growth Target as AI Reshapes Travel Tech
item.description: Amadeus has never committed to a multi-year earnings target before. Doing so now — while AI reshapes travel — raises a question the whole industry is watching: does value stay with the plumbing, or move to the interface?

item.title: Southwest Airlines Bars Employees From Wearing Smart Glasses: Scoop
item.description: Southwest is banning the use of wearable technology such as AI-powered smart glasses in the workplace. Sales of Meta’s smart glasses tripled over the last year.

item.title: FAA Considers Reducing Flights at Chicago O’Hare After American and United Turf War
item.description: After American and United significantly increased their schedules at O’Hare, the FAA is now looking to reduce flights at the airport this summer out of concern that the airport could face more strain.
